title: EventEnvelope
description: One row of the append-only event log: the record of what happened, in the order it happened. The log is what makes a plan explainable months later and what makes a derived metric re-computable after a bug fix (docs/data/event-catalog.md rule 1), so this contract specifies the envelope only. Payload shapes belong to the catalogue, one per event type, because a single schema holding 45 payload variants would either be strict about none of them or duplicate the catalogue and drift from it. Rows are never updated or deleted; corrections are new events that reference the superseded row.

eventId.description: Generated by the writer, not the client, so a replayed request cannot forge identity; the id is what a correction event points at with supersedesEventId.

userId.description: Present on every table and every document (AGENTS rule 7). Row-level security is the enforcement; this field is the audit that the enforcement has something to key on.

type.description: domain.action, past tense, camelCase in the action part (plan.diffStored, entry.submitted). Deliberately a pattern rather than an enum: the catalogue in docs/data/event-catalog.md is the list of truth, and an enum copied here would be a second list that drifts. An unknown type is caught by the replay fixtures, not by this schema. That is a known, stated gap, not an oversight.

occurredAt.description: The instant it happened, UTC, to millisecond precision. Never used to derive a training day on its own: the boundary is local and the offset is recorded per row for exactly that reason.

actor.description: Who is responsible for the fact. A runner's tap and a worker's nightly refinement must never look identical in the audit, because they carry different authority: only runner actions feed adherence and autonomy learning.

payloadVersion.description: Per-type payload version, integer, additive-only (docs/data/event-catalog.md rule 2). Readers ignore unknown fields and never guess a missing one.

payload.description: The type-specific body, camelCase keys, units in the names, documented in docs/data/event-catalog.md. Constrained by the envelope, not by a 45-way combinator here. Contains no free-text health content and nothing classified health-sensitive (ADR-0006): a pain note lives in pain_reports and is referenced by id, because logs are copied, exported and read by people debugging them.

trainingDay.description: The local training day this event belongs to, resolved at write time as [day 04:00, next day 04:00) in the user's zone. Stored rather than derived at read time, so that a user moving across timezones next year cannot silently rewrite which day their Tuesday run happened on.

timezone.description: IANA zone used to compute trainingDay, e.g. Asia/Taipei. Recorded per row: the rule that produced a stored fact is part of that fact.

dayStartHour.description: The training-day boundary hour in effect at write time (users.dayStartHour). Same argument as timezone: store the inputs of a derived value, or the derivation becomes unreproducible.

idempotencyKey.description: Set by the client for anything the network may retry, so a double-tap on the daily entry writes one event. Null for server-originated events, which cannot be retried by a client.

causationId.description: The event that caused this one: an accepted review option is the cause of the plan.generated and plan.activated events it produces. Without it the log is a list; with it, the log is a chain a runner can be shown.

supersedesEventId.description: For entry.corrected and similar: this row replaces that row's meaning. The old row stays, because deleting it would silently change every metric already computed from it (AGENTS rule 4).

schemaUrl.description: Optional pointer to the catalogue entry or contract this payload was written against, so a reader in 2029 can tell which revision of which rule produced this row.

allOf.description: A runner action always arrives over a network that retries, so it always carries an idempotency key; a null key on a runner action is a client bug and must fail at write time rather than duplicate a daily entry.

A day closes once, and the sweep is the only thing allowed to say so: a runner cannot close their own day, because that would let a tap decide whether the day counts as unlogged. The payload carries both what the plan asked and what was reported, so `closed-unlogged` is a status with a null outcome rather than a zero that looks like a decision.

Safety events are raised by the system, never by a tap, and an override records which flag it overrode. A safety event without a cause chain is the one audit gap that must never be possible (AGENTS rule 3).
